Bidar was a small sultanate in the northern Deccan of India, ruled from the walled city of Bidar from about 1492 to 1619. The city had earlier been the capital of the Bahmani Sultanate, which moved there from Gulbarga around 1429. The minister Mahmud Gawan built a great college there in 1472, and the Russian merchant Afanasy Nikitin described the city in those years.

When the Bahmani state broke apart, the Barid Shahi family, its last chief ministers, kept the capital and a strip of land around it. It was the smallest of the five Deccan sultanates. Bidar joined the alliance that crushed Vijayanagara at the battle of Talikota in 1565. In 1619 its neighbour Bijapur annexed it, though the map still shows it to 1650.
